title: arXiv:2605.04999
quoted_text: Even for event-free survival endpoints, individuals may avoid some components of a composite outcome (e.g., disease relapse) but not death itself. In these settings, cure models are best understood as capturing long-term survivorship rather than absolute immunity: the cure fraction is interpreted as the proportion of the population whose event hazard becomes negligible after a sufficient duration of follow-up.
